title: Four-Square Representations: Jacobi's Four-Square Theorem
description: Formalizes Jacobi's Four-Square Theorem (1834): r₄(n) = 8 × Σ_{d|n, 4∤d} d. Proves consequences: r₄(n) > 0 for all n > 0 (recovering Lagrange's theorem), exact values for small n, r₄(p) = 8(p+1) for odd primes p, and 8 | r₄(n) for all n > 0. Jacobi's formula requires modular forms (1 axiom); counting consequences proved. 45 theorems, 2 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Lagrange (1770) proved every positive integer is a sum of four squares. Jacobi (1834) gave the exact count r₄(n) via divisor sums.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize r₄(n) counting function and Jacobi's exact formula.
overview.proofStrategy: Define modified divisor sum σ*(n) = Σ_{d|n, 4∤d} d. Jacobi axiomatized (requires modular forms); consequences proved.
